building.also_note: no other building of the campus map: measured 2026-10-22 from the model's footprint (cells above 2.5 m, 0.5 m grid, run.sh topview) it covers 92.2% of 102's block and less than 0.5% of any other block within 80 m.
building.title: Old Government House, University of Auckland
building.note: outline: building 102's outline from the main project's campus.json, in the map's frame (equirectangular metres east/north of the origin, true north), not in the LiDAR frame (local NZTM). It is used only to choose the crop box and to draw on the heightmap figure; the frame comes from the LiDAR.

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north

door.note: view frame: the foot of the porch steps on the middle bay's axis (parts/main.js MIDDLE.axis, parts/bay.js PORCH), where the ground is `ground` m and the model's y is 0; place.py puts it on the map

frame.method: LiDAR building points (class 6): centre = mean x/y of points higher than tower_above m (the main roof's ridges); axis = principal axis of points between min_above and spine_below m high within spine_radius m of the centre: the upper roofs of the main block and its end wings, as min_above is the height of the eaves (lower, the service ranges behind turn it 10 deg off the garden front) (pointing south-east, as street_side is east); toStreet = the axis turned 90 deg toward street_side: north-east, to the lawn and the garden front of the main two-storey block, where most of the Google panoramas are. The lower service wings are on the south-west side (-z). Only building points inside the outline or within near_outline m of it count: another building stands in the crop box.

streetview.pano_ids_note: the only two Google panoramas that show the building (2025-05, on the campus road 72 and 82 m from its south-east end, through trees; 2026-10-22). The building stands in its grounds among large trees: of the 30 Google panoramas within 120 m, the other 28 see only trees (looked at in a low-resolution probe, zoom 3, 180 tiles). User-contributed panoramas are not used. So this landmark is checked as having no references for its silhouette (landmarks/README.md); these two show the upper storey of the south-east end and the garden front, in part.

light.note: the viewer's light for this building (pipeline/viewer/main.js; the address still wins): the sun of the two panoramas (2025-05), seen in hRE5's wide view at bearing about 337 deg and 32.5 deg up, about 13:30 NZST; 335/33 fits the shading of the garden front; a sunlit lawn below the horizon (ground, groundshade) lights the walls from below as in the photographs, measured surface by surface in the look agent's round 2
